[Model and example](../vignettes/04_action_selection/04_action_selection.ipynb) · [All benchmarks](../benchmark.qmd)

The model estimates **pass versus carry**, conditional on the current tracking
state. It does not predict whether the chosen action succeeds. Its native
XGBoost output is $\pi(s)=P(\mathrm{pass}\mid s)$; carrying has probability
$1-\pi(s)$. Together with the separate execution models this gives

$$
h(s)=[1-\pi(s)]\,P(\mathrm{loss\ within\ 1s}\mid\mathrm{carry},s)
      +\pi(s)\sum_jq_j(s)[1-p_j(s)],
$$

where $q_j$ is conditional pass-destination choice and $p_j$ is calibrated pass
completion at the hypothetical destination. The action model learns the
population's average choices, not an optimal policy or individual skill.
The [example vignette](../vignettes/04_action_selection/04_action_selection.ipynb)
defines every input and illustrates the joint outcome-weighted aggregates.

## Decisions, features and fold construction

The final cohort has **16,918 decisions: 7,770 passes and 9,148 carries**, from
the same ten matches. Carriers are outfield players, individual-control endpoints
are matched, and shot-ending individual possessions are excluded. Successful
carries are full one-second actions; failed carries remain choices even when
they fail before one second. Successful fractional tails and additional hazard
snapshots are excluded from action-choice training. A 2.4-second possession
ending with a pass gives choices at 0 and 1 s for carrying, and at 2.4 s for
passing; the 2-second snapshot is only for hazard evaluation. A pass after
0.4 s contributes the release choice, with the original start context.

Raw granular start/previous labels, including `unknown`, are retained. The
physical carry model's OBE loss-parent filter is **not** imposed on action
choices: choosing to carry and successfully executing it are separate tasks.
No future outcome, receiver, remaining duration, role or player identity enters.

There are **30 conceptual inputs: 28 numeric and two categorical**, grouped as
five context, six carrier/pressure, eight spatial/tactical and eleven pass-option
features. Context includes completed whole carries, not fractional possession
age. Carrier velocity uses speed and angle to attack. Spatial values include
own/opponent xT, nearest-line index/distance at the one-second carrier
projection, and current counts ahead of the carrier. Passing summaries combine
$q_j$ with calibrated $p_j$: expected completion, own-success/opponent-failure
xT, four line and four ahead-count aggregates. These are joint weighted sums,
not conditional branch means. Counts use the carrier team's attack direction
for both rosters; backward destinations can have more players ahead.

Five outer folds use **6 fit + 2 validation + 2 test matches**. Every state has
five versions of its learned inputs. For each action fold, pass-risk parameters,
physical carry parameters/bases, destination-choice utilities and xT come from
the same six fitting matches. Pass completion uses their separate two-match
isotonic transform; destination choice uses its saved two-match temperature and
raw pitch control internally. BCOS uses that fold's carry-arrival dispersion,
a 40 m domain, a 1 m target grid, 0.03125 m path spacing and 0.04 s temporal
integration. Full-data deployment fits never supply these benchmark features.
All stages use the final overspeed-preserving TTI where specified; the component
speed caps remain task-specific. See the [kinematic conventions](../docs/kinematic-parameter-conventions.md).

Fitting-state upstream scores are in-sample to their fitted component models.
The same two validation matches support upstream calibration, action tuning and
early stopping. This is a frozen component stack with an outer held-out test,
not independently nested tuning of every layer. These ten development matches
have also informed earlier experiments; no untouched external benchmark is claimed.

## Native likelihood and hyperparameter search

Each tree ensemble gives a score $f_\theta(z)$ and probability
$\pi=\operatorname{sigmoid}(f_\theta(z))$. Native `binary:logistic` minimizes
Bernoulli negative log-likelihood with tree regularization:

$$
-\sum_i\{y_i\log\pi_i+(1-y_i)\log(1-\pi_i)\}+\Omega(\theta),
\qquad y_i=1\text{ for pass},\quad y_i=0\text{ for carry}.
$$

The native score gradient is $\pi_i-y_i$ and its curvature is
$\pi_i(1-\pi_i)$. No custom categorical-choice derivatives or nests are used
for this binary task [@chen2016xgboost].

| Parameter | Tested values / setting | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| Maximum depth | 3, 4, 6, 8 | Compare modest through richer interactions. |
| Minimum child weight | 1, 5, 20 | Vary minimum Hessian support; this is not a fixed number of observations. |
| L2 leaf regularization | 0.1, 1, 3, 10 | Compare weak and stronger leaf-weight shrinkage. |
| Learning rate | 0.03, 0.05, 0.10 | Compare slower and faster learning within the same ceiling. |
| Trees / early stopping | At most 2,000 / patience 100 | Select the best validation prefix and report cap hits. |
| Row / column sampling | 0.8 / 0.8 | Fixed stochastic regularization across candidates. |
| Tree method | CPU `hist`, 256 bins | Efficient native training at this sample size. |
| Seed | 20261026 + fold; per-iteration sampling | Reproducible fold-specific sampling. |

These are project search ranges, not literature-derived optimal values. Their
meaning follows the [XGBoost parameter documentation](https://xgboost.readthedocs.io/en/stable/parameter.html).
All **144 configurations per fold, 720 fits**, are trained without progressive
screening or resampling. Vocabulary, one-hot columns and the native intercept
use fitting data only. Validation logloss selects configuration and tree prefix;
that selection is saved before opening test features. Missing/unseen categories
are explicit. No classifier calibration is used in the primary result.

| Fold | Depth | Child weight | L2 | Learning rate | Selected trees |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 0 | 4 | 5 | 3 | 0.03 | 541 |
| 1 | 8 | 1 | 10 | 0.03 | 217 |
| 2 | 6 | 5 | 1 | 0.05 | 186 |
| 3 | 4 | 1 | 0.1 | 0.03 | 419 |
| 4 | 8 | 20 | 3 | 0.03 | 248 |

Every candidate early-stopped below the ceiling. Selected held-out predictions
were independently replayed from the saved ensembles, with maximum probability
difference 1.20e-7. [Selected configurations](../data/benchmarks/action_selection/selected_configurations.csv)
and [encoded schemas](../data/benchmarks/action_selection/feature_schemas.json).

## Pooled results and published comparisons

Pooled evaluation concatenates each held-out decision once. Null probabilities
are the corresponding six-fit pass proportions. CE uses natural logarithms;
ECE uses ten equal-count rank bins, recalculated on the pooled scores.

| Model | CE | Null CE | Gain over null | Brier | AUC | Quantile ECE |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| **PRESS, native XGBoost** | **0.568592** | **0.690053** | **17.602%** | **0.193975** | **0.77083** | **1.026%** |
| Temperature diagnostic only | 0.568411 | 0.690053 | 17.628% | 0.193872 | 0.77092 | 0.817% |

Held-out fold gains range from **16.20% to 19.02%**. Pooled ECE is not the
average of fold ECE. [Pooled metrics](../data/benchmarks/action_selection/metrics.csv),
[per-fold scores](../data/benchmarks/action_selection/metrics_by_fold.csv),
[per-match scores](../data/benchmarks/action_selection/metrics_by_match.csv).

![Action selection: pooled five-fold calibration and native signed bin deviations. Each bin contains 1,691 or 1,692 held-out decisions. The temperature curve is a separate diagnostic, not the selected benchmark output.](../figures/action_selection_pooled_calibration.png){#fig-action-selection-calibration}

The native curve is close to the diagonal: average absolute bin deviation is
**1.03 percentage points**, with maximum bin deviation about **2.41 points**.
This does not establish perfect pointwise or subgroup calibration. ECE depends
on binning and sample size; no universal 1% acceptance threshold is assumed.

| Published binary action-choice model | CE | Null CE | Gain over null |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Stalpaert, major previous-action categories | 0.5762 | 0.6602 | 12.72% |
| PRESS, native final development benchmark | 0.568592 | 0.690053 | 17.60% |
| Stalpaert, specific previous-action types included | 0.4807 | 0.6602 | 27.19% |

Stalpaert explicitly uses **human-annotated action types**, alongside seven broad
categories, and reports the large benefit of the specific types in §4.6/Table4.6.
Those inputs cannot be reproduced from our provider labels without equivalent
annotations. PRESS is numerically between these two references; differing data,
prevalence, features and validation prevent a controlled superiority claim.
Stalpaert's Table4.7 reports postcalibration action ECE 2.17%; it is not assigned
to both uncalibrated Table4.6 variants here [@stalpaert2022].
[Published values and locators](../data/benchmarks/action_selection/literature_comparison.csv).
Fernández motivates the action decomposition and one-second carry convention,
but its **shoot/pass/carry** classifier has a different label space and is not
a direct numerical baseline for this binary task [@fernandez2021].

The historical PRESS gain of **15.965%** used 17,677 decisions. Relative to it,
the current cohort excludes 1,094 goalkeeper decisions and recovers 335 otherwise
valid decisions with unknown context; 16,583 decisions overlap. Splits and
upstream feature fitting also changed. The difference cannot be attributed
solely to richer features or BCOS.
[Exact cohort audit](../data/benchmarks/action_selection/historical_cohort_comparison.json).

## Small context and calibration diagnostics

Origin of the verified team-possession chain and its previously completed pass
count were tested separately and together. All original inputs were reused;
each fold's selected hyperparameters stayed fixed, with fresh paired baseline
fits and the same early-stopping procedure. Across three seeds, origin adds
**0.105 percentage points** of null gain on average, count **0.039**, and both
**0.053**. Both together range from -0.056 to +0.148 points. Chains with missing
links retain unresolved origin and conservative verified-pass counts; no rows
are removed. This modest, variable gain does not justify expanding the selected
feature set. Local baselines were freshly refitted and not bit-identical to
cluster training; these changes are relative to each paired local baseline,
not a revision of the frozen 17.602% result.
[All seed comparisons](../data/benchmarks/action_selection/context_probe_by_seed.csv)
and [summary](../data/benchmarks/action_selection/context_probe_summary.csv).

A separate inexpensive check fits one positive temperature per frozen fold:
$\pi_T=\operatorname{sigmoid}[\operatorname{logit}(\pi)/T]$. It minimizes
Bernoulli NLL on the existing two validation matches, never test ECE; the
underlying trees remain fixed [@guo2017calibration]. Temperatures are
**1.0875, 1.0256, 1.0279, 1.0153 and 1.0537**. Pooled ECE improves from
1.026% to 0.817%, while CE changes by only -0.000180 and gain by +0.026 points.
The native output remains the primary model. This is a post-development
diagnostic reusing validation already used for selection, not an independent
calibration holdout or a test-selected deployment rule.
[Temperature values](../data/benchmarks/action_selection/temperature_diagnostic.csv).

## Production refit and public example

The package now loads **`skillcorner_outfield_action_selection_v2`**, the verified
full-ten-match native XGBoost refit: **16,918 decisions, 277 trees, no classifier
scaling**. Its single configuration minimizes mean validation CE across the five
AS70 grids: depth6, child weight1, L2=10, learning rate0.03. For that same
configuration the five best prefixes are242/329/369/253/277; their median277
fixes the deployment tree count. No outer-test score selects these values.
These are deployment rules, not a new held-out performance result.

All production feature inputs use the full-data pass-risk, carry-risk, flat
destination-choice and xT artifacts. BCOS uses full-data carry s=0.2996318905,
with the same verified numerical convention; no fold model or averaged fold
coefficient supplies these production features. The existing full-data raw-PC
cache is reused for6,808 identical states, and the remaining10,110 are computed.

The export independently replays the full17k model matrix and200 native-grid
feature fixtures through the public reader, with **zero probability and feature
differences**. The revised runtime retains raw unknown/missing context, integer
past-carry counts, signed line distances and the agreed4+4 aggregates. BCOS
returns a probability field and its probability-weighted **area in m²**; use
`BCOS area` as the scalar input. Old weights and code are archived together.

The [example](../vignettes/04_action_selection/04_action_selection.ipynb) now calls
this installed model on a synthetic frame and uses the package pitch plot.
Coarse example grids remain illustrative. Reported benchmark scores and the
pooled calibration curve still come from AS70 held-out predictions, not the
full-data refit's training scores.
[Refit and runtime provenance](../docs/action-selection-refit-provenance.json),
[benchmark source hashes](../docs/action-selection-benchmark-provenance.json).
